sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Imports the file checks, the test runner, the persona list and the switchboard functions.
sections.why: Provides the tools the roster tests need.

sections.name: roster: personas
sections.title: Persona files
sections.what: Checks there are five personas with fixed public names, each with a card file and a playbook. Checks each playbook has the AI analyst label, the voice rules, the vocabulary section and the never section, and that it does not contain a list of real people's names.
sections.why: Likely reason: every persona must be clearly labelled as AI and must not use real identities.
sections.watch_out: The name check is a text match, so it may miss variations of the names.

sections.name: roster: Persona Switchboard
sections.title: Switchboard voicings
sections.what: Checks the switchboard example is labelled as illustrative and not a real match, that there are five voicings, that each has the same numbers as the facts, that the opening sentences are all different, and that the facts are model estimates from one engine with the first higher than the second.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same verified numbers must appear in every voice, so no persona changes the facts.
sections.watch_out: Number matching compares text, so changing how a number is formatted can cause a false failure.

summary: Tests the persona roster: the five analyst personas, their written guides, and the switchboard that restates the same verified facts in each persona's voice.
purpose: Keeps the five personas consistent, clearly labelled as AI, and free of real people's names, and makes sure every voice uses the same numbers.
why: Likely reason: personas present analysis to users, so they must be labelled, consistent with the facts, and must not borrow real names.
how: Checks each persona has a public name, a card file and a playbook with the required sections and the AI analyst label, and that the playbook has no real names. Then checks the switchboard labels its example as illustrative, gives five voicings that share the same numbers, and uses five different opening sentences.
inputs: Persona files in the personas folder and the switchboard's example facts.
risks: The name check is a plain text match, so spelling variants could pass. Number matching compares text, so formatting such as trailing zeros can cause a false failure.
debug: Check the failing persona folder for its card and playbook. For number mismatches, compare the exact text of each voicing with the facts.
